brief.headline: Memory supercycle accelerating—Q2 DRAM +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% QoQ, HBM3E +20% on full allocation; hyperscaler capex hits $700B in 2026
brief.summary: <cite index="13-2,13-7">Conventional DRAM contract prices will rise 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, while NAND Flash contract prices will jump 70-75% QoQ, following Q1's record 90-95% DRAM surge.</cite> <cite index="5-1">Samsung and SK Hynix hiked HBM3E prices nearly 20% for 2026 deliveries as demand for AI accelerators outstrips supply.</cite> <cite index="22-5,22-9">Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, and Alphabet collectively will spend roughly $700 billion on capital expenditures in 2026, nearly double 2025.</cite> <cite index="33-1,33-3">TSMC's CoWoS capacity is expected to reach 115,000 to 140,000 wafers per month by end of 2026, increasing to approximately 170,000 wafers per month in 2027.</cite> <cite index="41-5,41-6">KB Securities reports customer memory demand fulfillment is only about 50%, with packaging substrate lead times rising fourfold from 6 weeks to 24 weeks.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="40-5">SK Hynix held a 53% HBM market share in Q3 2025, compared to Samsung's 35%.</cite> <cite index="41-9">SK Hynix Q2 operating profit is estimated to have increased eightfold YoY to 69 trillion won (operating margin of 77%), while Samsung's Q2 operating profit is estimated to have soared 19-fold YoY to 90 trillion won (operating margin of 51%).</cite> SK Hynix maintains superior HBM positioning and margin profile (77% vs 51%), but Samsung's larger absolute profit delta and recent HBM4 customer feedback ("Samsung is back") narrows the gap. Prefer SK Hynix on memory purity and allocation dominance, but Samsung's catch-up trajectory reduces relative alpha. Both benefit from supply allocation chokepoint through 2027.

memory_cycle.stage: Mid-cycle acceleration with structural supply constraint
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="10-2,10-3">Q1 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices increased 55-60% QoQ, while NAND Flash prices rose 33-38% QoQ, driven by widening supply-demand gap particularly in server-related segments as cloud service providers secure capacity.</cite> <cite index="1-6">Meaningful new DRAM capacity unlikely to come online until 2027 at the earliest.</cite> <cite index="10-4,10-5">DRAM manufacturers are reallocating advanced process nodes and new capacity toward server DRAM and HBM to support growing AI server demand, significantly constraining supply to other applications.</cite> <cite index="1-10">SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won noted HBM carries margins around 60%, while standard memory chips reach roughly 80%.</cite> Pricing power remains with suppliers; no near-term relief.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="4-4">HBM3 ~$200/stack, HBM3E ~$300/stack, HBM4 ~$500/stack per April 2026 Silicon Analysts pricing.</cite> <cite index="4-8,4-10">For the B200 with eight HBM3e stacks, memory alone costs $2,400 exceeding logic die cost; SK Hynix and Samsung are expanding capacity at Icheon, Cheongju, and Pyeongtaek fabs, but demand from NVIDIA, AMD, and hyperscalers continues to outpace available production.</cite> <cite index="4-11">Lead times for HBM3E stacks remain at 20-26 weeks.</cite> <cite index="31-9">NVIDIA reportedly securing over 60% of total CoWoS capacity for 2025 and 2026.</cite> <cite index="32-2,32-6">A surge of AI and HPC orders from NVIDIA, Google, Amazon, and MediaTek has driven TSMC's entire CoWoS lineup to full capacity, with both CoWoS-L and CoWoS-S fully booked.</cite> HBM remains the primary supply gating factor for AI accelerators through 2027; memory cost share of total BOM rising to 30-40%.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscalers to spend ~$700B on AI capex in 2026, up nearly 2x YoY
news_pulse.implication: Unprecedented demand for GPUs, HBM, server DRAM/NAND. Samsung/SK Hynix selling into multi-year allocation agreements with hyperscalers at elevated ASPs. Validates aggressive capex plans and pricing power through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contract prices +58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, NAND +70-75% QoQ (TrendForce)
news_pulse.implication: Q2 price increases following Q1's +90-95% DRAM surge. Suppliers reallocating capacity to HBM and server products; meaningful fab expansion not until late 2027. Margin expansion continues for Samsung/SK Hynix through 2026.

news_pulse.headline: KB Securities: Memory demand fulfillment only 50%, packaging substrate lead times 4x to 24 weeks
news_pulse.implication: Dual bottleneck: memory wafer supply and back-end packaging. Samsung/SK Hynix unable to meet full customer demand despite record utilization. Supports pricing power and validates substrate/CoWoS tightness.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix hiked HBM3E prices ~20% for 2026 deliveries
news_pulse.implication: Rare HBM price increase as manufacturers pivot production toward HBM4, creating supply crunch for current-gen HBM3E. Reinforces allocation advantage for Samsung/SK Hynix and validates premium pricing.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity to reach 115-140K wafers/month by end-2026, 170K in 2027
news_pulse.implication: TSMC expanding CoWoS but still fully booked through 2026-27 with NVIDIA, Google, Amazon. Advanced packaging remains gating item for AI accelerators; benefits Samsung/SK Hynix HBM allocation as packaging supply grows.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung P5 fab operational by 2028, SK Hynix M15X by mid-2027
news_pulse.implication: New DRAM wafer capacity timeline confirms supply tightness through 2027. Samsung and SK Hynix signed OpenAI LOI for 900K DRAM wafers/month for Stargate. Long-term capacity secured but pricing tailwind persists near-term.

news_pulse.headline: 3x leveraged Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix ETPs listed on London Stock Exchange June 12
news_pulse.implication: New derivatives products (SMG3, HNX3 tickers) provide 3x long exposure via KRX futures. Increases foreign flow channel and derivatives volume; watch for volatility amplification and potential gamma effects on underlying KRX futures.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix 53% HBM market share Q3 2025 vs Samsung 35%; Q2 2026 OP estimates 69T won (77% margin) vs Samsung 90T won (51% margin)
news_pulse.source: Counterpoint / KB Securities via Asia Business Daily
news_pulse.implication: SK Hynix maintains HBM leadership and superior margin profile. Samsung absolute profit larger due to scale/foundry mix, but memory segment margin gap signals SK Hynix's allocation premium. Both set for Q2 earnings beats.

brief.derivatives_signal: <cite index="37-2,37-3">SK Hynix call/put ratio hits extremes with calls outnumbering puts 100:1, 1-month ATM IV near 130%, and July call OI concentrated in deep ITM strikes; 3x leveraged ETPs (SMG3/HNX3) listed on LSE June 12.</cite> <cite index="37-5">AUM of 2x single stock leveraged ETF products for Samsung and SK Hynix increased 87% from May 27 to 9.8 trillion won on June 12.</cite> Extreme retail positioning and IV; new 3x LSE products route foreign flow via KRX futures, adding gamma/convexity risk. Short-term overextended but fundamentals support. Monitor LSE ETP flows and KRX futures open interest for institutional hedging activity.
watch_for_next_3h: KRX futures volume/open interest on Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix post-LSE 3x ETP launch (June 12)
Hyperscaler Q2 earnings commentary on memory allocation and HBM supply constraints (Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon late June-early July)
TSMC CoWoS capacity update and NVIDIA Blackwell packaging mix commentary (CoWoS-L transition)
Samsung/SK Hynix preliminary Q2 earnings guidance (typically mid-July); consensus OP Samsung 90T won, SK Hynix 69T won
